newsitem.title: JAPAN: NKK aims for 1999/2000 parent profit of 65 bln yen.
newsitem.headline: NKK aims for 1999/2000 parent profit of 65 bln yen.

text.p: NKK Corp said on Tuesday the company was targeting parent current profits of 65 billion yen on sales of 1.3 trillion yen in the 1999/2000 business year.
The company also said it was aiming for group sales of more than two trillion yen in the business year ending March 31, 2000.

Last Thursday, NKK revised down its forecast for parent current profit in 1996/97 to 34 billion yen from a November forecast of 40 billion yen and against an actual 30.30 billion yen a year earlier. It revised up its sales forecast to 1.2 trillion yen from a November forecast of 1.19 trillion yen and against an actual 1.17 trillion yen.

To achieve the projected profit and sales figures in 1999/2000, the major Japanese steelmaker plans to continue cost-cutting efforts and technological development, and to strengthen it sales activities.
Under the three-year programme, NKK plans to strengthen its steel products business, an NKK spokesman said.

The 1.3 trillion yen sales target comprised 700 billion yen from the steel division, little changed from the present level, and 600 billion yen from the engineering division, up from the current 400 billion yen, the spokesman said.
